title: Billing Policy Statement: Requisition Encounters on Laboratory Test Orders
content:
## 1. The requisition encounter

All Laboratory Test Orders of the same patient that carry the same requisition number form one **requisition encounter**.

## 2. Requisitions spanning several service classes

A requisition that lists tests of more than one service class is accessioned as one order per service class. Every one of those orders carries the shared requisition number, and each test is placed on the order whose service-class test menu lists it.

## 3. The consumer physician oversight fee

The consumer physician oversight fee is charged once per requisition encounter. It is charged on the order of the encounter whose service class has the lowest rank, at that class's consumer physician oversight fee; the other orders of the encounter carry no oversight fee line. The service classes rank as follows:

| Rank | Service class |
|---|---|
| 1 | Routine Clinical Testing |
| 2 | Specialty Clinical Testing |
| 3 | Esoteric Reference Testing |
| 4 | Molecular Infectious Disease Testing |
| 5 | Clinical Toxicology Testing |
| 6 | Anatomic Pathology & Cytology |
| 7 | Hereditary & Reproductive Genetic Testing |

**Worked example (hypothetical).** A patient buys, on one consumer-initiated requisition, a Vitamin B12 (a Routine Clinical Testing test) and a Trichomonas vaginalis RNA test (a Molecular Infectious Disease Testing test). The requisition becomes two orders sharing one requisition number, and together they are one requisition encounter. Routine Clinical Testing has the lower rank (1 against 4), so the single oversight fee line sits on the Routine Clinical Testing order, at that class's oversight fee; the Molecular Infectious Disease Testing order carries no oversight fee line.

## 4. Retired clause on estimates

> *No longer in force.* The former clause read: "A good faith estimate is issued per requisition encounter, never per order: its amount is the sum, over every order of the encounter, of the self-pay price in that order's test menu of each test currently charged and not credited on the order, plus the consumer physician oversight fee once when the encounter is consumer-initiated; the same amount and the same estimate date are written to every order of the encounter."

This clause is no longer in force: it has been superseded by the current basis for good faith estimates and no longer governs how an estimate is calculated or where it is written. Sections 1 to 3 remain in force.
